title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes titled 'Chirurgie conforme', dated 11.1.84. A conformal surface with boundary is defined by local charts modelled on the closed upper half-plane H̄ = {Im z ≥ 0}. Theorem 1 (previous page) says the conformal structure of such a surface X is determined by its structure on Int(X). Equivalently, the structure sheaf can be recovered as the sheaf of continuous complex functions that are holomorphic in the interior.

This page proves Theorem 1. It characterises the boundary charts U → H̄ as exactly the topological charts (open topological embeddings sending boundary to boundary) that are conformal on Int U. The key step is Lemma 1. Let U be open in H̄ and let f: U ↪ H̄ be an open embedding (mapping U∩ℝ into ℝ) that is holomorphic on U∩H. Then f is holomorphic up to the boundary: near each point of U∩ℝ it extends holomorphically to a neighbourhood in ℂ.

Grothendieck derives this from the Schwarz reflection principle (he calls it 'lemme de Schwarz'). A continuous function on U, holomorphic on U∩H and real on U∩ℝ, extends holomorphically across ℝ.

To finish he must show the extended germ at a boundary point x is invertible, so that f is a genuine holomorphic chart. Expand f(z) − f(x) = a_n (z−x)^n + … with n > 0 and a_n ≠ 0. The next page notes that injectivity, together with H mapping into H, forces n = 1. Indeed, the reflected extension is injective near x, so its local degree is 1.

The next page goes on to two things. First, Theorem 2: compact bordered conformal surfaces are equivalent to smooth proper real algebraic curves, via the Schottky/Klein double. Second, Theorem 3: cutting a conformal surface along a sufficiently regular 1-complex K yields a bordered conformal surface. The purpose is to lay foundations for 'conformal surgery', i.e. cutting and gluing Riemann surfaces along curves.
errors: The 'lemme de Schwarz' invoked is really the Schwarz reflection principle, not the Schwarz lemma.

Lemma 1 as written omits an explicit hypothesis. f must map U∩ℝ into ℝ (boundary to boundary), which reflection needs. It is stated in the preceding characterisation ('plongeant bord dans bord') and follows for open embeddings into H̄ by invariance of domain, so this is a minor gap only.
Invertibility of the germ is deferred to the next page (n = 1 argument). That argument is correct: the reflected extension is locally injective, hence has nonzero derivative.

ideas.what: A bordered Riemann surface's structure is determined by its interior structure. Boundary charts are exactly the boundary-preserving topological charts that are holomorphic inside.
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness of the conformal structure on a bordered Riemann surface / boundary regularity via reflection

ideas.what: Lemma 1: an open embedding into H̄ that is holomorphic in the interior extends holomorphically across the real boundary.
The extended germ is invertible because an injective holomorphic germ has order-1 leading term.
ideas.modern_name: Local degree / univalence implies nonvanishing derivative

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a routine foundational verification: reflection plus a local injectivity argument. The only historical interest is that Grothendieck in 1984 was carefully setting up foundations for conformal surgery, in the spirit of Esquisse d'un programme. The mathematics itself is classical.
transcription_corrections: '𝔅U (i.e. de H)' is likely '∂U' or 'Ū', meaning a holomorphic chart of the bordered structure at x; the glyph is unclear.
'lemme de Schwarz' is correctly transcribed from the image, but it refers to the reflection principle.

The final line probably reads something like 'Mais on a pour ce germe un développement en série...' followed by 'par continuité'. It continues on the next page with 'une série qui commence par a_n z^n'.
'H̄^+' in the first line and in Lemma 1 likely just denotes H̄, the closed upper half-plane.
